# Theme Development

EComposer lets you build web pages quickly and flexibly. It also lets developers create **custom elements** and plug them into the builder, where they work just like the built-in elements.

With custom elements you can:

- Build elements that fit the exact needs of your theme or store.
- Keep your pages unique and consistent with your brand.
- Ship your elements together with your theme.

## Prerequisites

To develop custom elements, you need basic knowledge of:

- HTML, CSS and JavaScript
- Vue
- Liquid

## Set up your theme

The Shopify theme code editor only allows certain file types in each folder, so custom element files go in the **assets** folder.

1. In your Shopify admin, go to **Online Store**, click the three dots (**...**) and select **Edit code**.

   <img src="/theme-editor.png" alt="Open the theme code editor" />

2. Expand the **assets** folder and click **Add a new asset**.
3. Extract the zip file below and upload all its files to your theme.

   <img src="/upload-assets.png" alt="Upload files to the assets folder" />

## File structure

A custom element needs two files in your theme's **assets** folder:

| File                      | Purpose                                      |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `ecomposer.json`          | Lists all the elements you have built.       |
| `MyComponent.ecom.liquid` | The code of one element (template + script). |

## 1. Register elements: `ecomposer.json`

Define every element you build in this file.

```json
{
  "author": "Kalles",
  "logo": "https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0332/6420/5963/files/kalles.svg",
  "website": "https://ecomposer.io?utm_source=ecomposer",
  "elements": {
    "MyComponent": {
      "types": ["home", "product", "page", "section", "quickview"],
      "name": "my-ecomponent",
      "title": "My Component",
      "file": "MyComponent.ecom.liquid",
      "icon": "<svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" fill=\"none\" viewBox=\"0 0 24 24\" stroke=\"currentColor\"><path stroke-linecap=\"round\" stroke-linejoin=\"round\" stroke-width=\"2\" d=\"M4 16l4.586-4.586a2 2 0 012.828 0L16 16m-2-2l1.586-1.586a2 2 0 012.828 0L20 14m-6-6h.01M6 20h12a2 2 0 002-2V6a2 2 0 00-2-2H6a2 2 0 00-2 2v12a2 2 0 002 2z\" /></svg>",
      "category": ["theme"],
      "data": {
        "title": "Test element",
        "settings": {
          "title": "Hello"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Element fields

| Field      | Description                                                                      |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `author`   | Your name or brand name.                                                         |
| `logo`     | URL of your logo.                                                                |
| `website`  | URL of your website.                                                             |
| `types`    | Page types where the element is available (`home`, `product`, `page`, ...).      |
| `name`     | Unique element name (lowercase, no spaces).                                      |
| `title`    | Name shown in the builder.                                                       |
| `file`     | The element file in the assets folder.                                           |
| `icon`     | SVG icon shown in the builder.                                                   |
| `category` | Group of the element in the builder.                                             |
| `data`     | Default content and settings used when the element is added to a page.           |

## 2. Write the element: `MyComponent.ecom.liquid`

An element file has two parts: a Vue `<template>` for the markup and a `<script>` for the logic.

```html
<template>
  <div>
    <h3 v-html="data?.settings?.title"></h3>
    <p>
      Lorem ipsum dolor, sit amet consectetur adipisicing elit. Minus molestiae
      ea neque, a alias dicta beatae reprehenderit necessitatibus asperiores
      ipsa nesciunt optio qui tempore animi enim sint! Quos, placeat similique!
    </p>
    <h3 v-html="liquid('setting_title')"></h3>
    <component
      :is="'script'"
      class="ecomposer-data"
      type="application/json"
      v-html="liquid('settings')"
    />
  </div>
</template>

<script>
export default {
  name: "My app",
  props: {
    data: {
      type: Object,
      default() {
        return {};
      },
    },
  },
  computed: {
    // Fields shown in the element settings panel
    settings() {
      return [
        {
          type: "text",
          name: "title",
          label: "Title",
        },
      ];
    },
    // Liquid code that runs on the storefront
    liquids() {
      return {
        settings: {
          code: `{{shop.metafields.ecomposer.my-app.value | json}}`,
          preview: "",
        },
        setting_title: {
          code: `{{shop.metafields.ecomposer.my-app.value.title}}`,
          preview: "",
        },
      };
    },
    // JavaScript that runs on the storefront
    javascript() {
      return function () {
        const $el = this.$el;
        const app_settings = $el.querySelector(".ecomposer-data");
        console.log(app_settings.innerHTML);
      };
    },
  },
  mounted() {
    // Set default settings when the element is added
    if (!this.data?.settings) {
      this.data.settings = {
        title: "Hello",
      };
    }
  },
};
</script>
```

### What each part does

- **`props.data`**: the element's saved content and settings.
- **`computed.settings`**: the list of fields merchants can edit in the builder.
- **`computed.liquids`**: Liquid snippets rendered by Shopify. Read the result in the template with `liquid('key')`. Use `preview` for the text shown inside the builder.
- **`computed.javascript`**: a function that runs on the storefront. Use `this.$el` to access the element's root node.
- **`mounted`**: runs when the element loads. Use it to set default values.
